title: The homelessness department’s own dashboards, November 2026
question: What do the department’s public dashboards say about empty beds, empty homes and results, and do they agree with each other and with the cases?
finding: Shelter: 3,058 of 3,396 beds occupied on 20 November 2026 (91%). Supportive housing: 92% occupied in July-August 2026; the inventory lists 9,649 site-based units, 451 more than the vacancy dashboard counts. Every scorecard target reads 'under review'. The exits page prints the same fiscal-year-to-date total for this year and last.
how: Numbers are read from the printed text of each dashboard page; each row names the page. Comparisons are with the vacancy dashboard read in the site’s “Rolls, Homekey and empty supportive housing” page and with the cases.
limits: Printed dashboards carry the figures on screen only, not the data behind them, and several charts printed without their tables. The inventory and the vacancy dashboard may count units differently (for example units not yet open or held for transfers). Unique-person totals are lower than the sum of months, so a monthly table cannot check them exactly.

rows.compare: The vacancy dashboard counted 9,198 site-based units on 12 Nov 2026; the inventory counts 451 more.
Site-based and scattered-site supportive housing, rapid re-housing and the housing ladder.
A 92% occupancy rate is 8% empty, in line with the vacancy dashboard's 8.3%; target shown as 'under review'.
51 sites, 3,396 beds, 3,058 occupied (91%): 338 beds empty on the night. The table under it lists only 3 site types (30 sites, one row printing 0 sites for 392 beds).

rows.measure: Exits since 1 Jul 2023 toward the 30,000 goal
rows.compare: The page shows 1,279 for this fiscal year to date and 1,279 for last year's same quarter, identical, while its monthly table adds to 1,331 and 1,335 (unique people are fewer than the sum of months, but identical totals are worth asking about).

Site-based supportive housing 1,423, scattered-site 249, rapid re-housing 753, housing ladder 104. The homelessness-money case counts 1,684 moved into supportive housing in fiscal 2026; this page gives 1,672.

rows.measure: Assessed this year and sent to a housing referral
rows.compare: 24% of those assessed; the rest were placed in 'problem solving'.
